Thanks for the quick intro earlier. Atlas Analytics is evaluating a semantic search + recommendation use case and we need to make sure cost and model choices line up before moving to a POC. A few questions up front so procurement and engineering can estimate:

- Do you price embeddings per-vector (per call / per vector returned) or per-token? If per-vector, is there any adjustment based on dimensionality (e.g., are 1536-d vectors priced differently than 2048/4096)?
- Which embeddings models do you currently support on the hosted API and what are their default output dimensions (and typical latency for a batch of 1k texts)?
- Do you have a published rate card for embeddings (including bulk ingestion / committed discounts)? Please attach if available.
- For pre-computing 1M vectors, what are the recommended approaches and any one-time ingestion costs we should expect?

If you can send a short rate card and call out any model-dim tradeoffs, procurement can start a baseline budget. We may ask for a committed volume discount if the numbers look good.

Samir —

Great questions. I attached our current embeddings rate card (PDF) and a very short SOW template for ingest + support. Quick answers below, with Rishi copied for any deep technical clarifications.

- Billing unit: hosted embeddings are billed per-vector (a single vector output counts as 1 unit). We do not bill per-token for embeddings; token-based billing applies only to text generation endpoints.
- Dimensions: price is not directly charged by raw dimension count, but we publish model-specific unit prices. In practice, higher-dimension models map to higher per-vector price (we normalize to per-vector to keep billing predictable).
- Supported models (hosted): redwood-embed-1-small (768d), redwood-embed-1-large (2048d), open-embedding-ada-002 (1536d) — all available in hosted API. See the rate card for model-specific per-vector prices and latency guidance.
- Bulk/precompute: ingestion is just hosted API calls for embeddings; compute cost follows the per-vector price. For large one-time ingests we commonly offer a phased ingestion plan and can provide a temporary ingestion credit / discounted batch pricing as part of a committed volume agreement.

I'll summarize ballpark list prices in my next reply (and Rishi will drop in with more detail). If procurement wants, we can follow up with a 30-min call to go over exact numbers and an outline for a committed discount.

Samir — quick technical breakdown to help procurement's cost table. Short version: hosted billing = per-vector units; we do not meter by raw token count for embeddings, but we have model-specific unit prices. Storage/hosting is a separate add-on. Details below: 

1) Billing mechanics (hosted embeddings):
- Each successful embedding call that returns N vectors is billed as N vector-units at the selected model's per-vector price. Example: a batch call that returns 1k vectors = 1000 billed units.
- Pre-compute of 1M vectors = 1M billed units (assuming host API calls to compute them). No separate "ingest tax" by default — ingestion is just API usage.

2) Model → dims → published per-vector list prices (public list; volume discounts can be applied):
- redwood-embed-1-small (768d): $0.00035 / vector
- open-embedding-ada-002 (1536d): $0.00040 / vector
- redwood-embed-1-large (2048d): $0.00120 / vector

(These are list prices — committed volume tiers reduce the effective per-vector cost. We typically offer: 10% off at $50k/month, 20% off at $150k/month, and custom pricing for enterprise reserved capacity.)

3) Storage / managed vector store:
- Redwood offers a managed vector store add-on for hosted customers (optional). Pricing: $0.20 / GB / month for storage + $0.00002 / query for hosted index serving (sample numbers — final SOW will list precise tiers). You can also persist indexes in your own cloud storage and point our runtime at it.

4) Ingestion throughput & latency guidance (hosted):
- Throughput for batch ingestion: typically 50–150 vectors/sec per vCPU shard depending on model; larger models are slower. Expect ~100–400 ms per vector for redwood-embed-1-large in typical latency profiles when called at small batch sizes; batching improves amortized latency.

5) Committed/Reserved options:
- For predictable costs at scale we support Dedicated pools and reserved capacity contracts (monthly commits). Those provide both lower per-vector compute pricing and custom SLAs for latency/throughput. We can include a one-time ingestion discount as part of the committed deal.

I'll prepare a 1M / 5M cost table at list prices + example discount tiers and send it shortly. If you want numbers for a specific model mix, tell me the split (e.g., 70% small, 30% large) and I'll run it.

—Rishi
